answer: Rotating beacon-lagoon schedule. Each agent must solve a fresh, agent-specific challenge derived from a time-varying beacon and a hidden lagoon seed known only to the verifier, then submit before a narrow window closes. The challenge binds identity to a specific slot; replaying or duplicating it fails. An attacker must run one live execution per identity per slot, paying continuous compute and coordination costs plus missed slots from a velvet timeout that voids stale submissions, so mass duplication becomes infeasible.
